standard_prerequisites.name: Adjunction between pullback and pushforward of modules on ringed topoi, at the level of complexes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Modules on Sites, the adjunction Hom_{K(O_D)}(F^bullet, f_* I^bullet) = Hom_{K(O_C)}(f^* F^bullet, I^bullet)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of hom groups with which the counted proof concludes.

core_obligations: Apply the adjunction (proof lines 4603-4608): for every complex F^bullet of O_D-modules, the adjunction identifies Hom_{K(O_D)}(F^bullet, f_* I^bullet) with Hom_{K(O_C)}(f^* F^bullet, I^bullet).

Use exactness of the pullback (proof lines 4609-4612): because f is flat, f^* is exact, so acyclic F^bullet are carried to acyclic f^* F^bullet and the identification passes to homotopy categories as displayed.
Conclude K-injectivity (proof lines 4612-4613): since I^bullet is K-injective, the right hand side is acyclic in F^bullet, hence so is the left hand side, which is the K-injectivity of f_* I^bullet.
proof_roadmap: Test K-injectivity of f_* I^bullet against homotopy classes of maps from complexes F^bullet.
Use the pullback-pushforward adjunction to rewrite those hom groups over the source topos.
Exactness of f^* identifies the relevant classes, so acyclicity transfers from I^bullet to f_* I^bullet.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a flat morphism of ringed topoi the pushforward of a K-injective complex is again K-injective (statement lines 4592-4600). The proof is a single adjunction computation: K-injectivity is tested by the acyclicity of Hom_{K(O_D)}(F^bullet, f_* I^bullet) in F^bullet, the pullback-pushforward adjunction rewrites that group as Hom_{K(O_C)}(f^* F^bullet, I^bullet), and exactness of f^* given by flatness is what makes the acyclicity transfer (proof lines 4603-4613). The non-formal point is that the flatness hypothesis enters exactly here. The claim is H2: one adjunction identification, with the cited adjunction coming from another chapter.
